meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

instrumental of вечер used as an adverb

examples.trans: I'm at home in the evening.

meanings.note: важный вопрос = an important matter
важный вопрос = an important matter

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Много дел = a lot to do. Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: followed by the genitive plural: 'десять минут'

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Contrast дома = at home. Core Russian adv meaning '(to) home, homeward' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: And you go home and do your homework.

examples.text: Так, мы идём к слепым. А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: Right, we're going to the blind people. And you go home and do your homework.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.
Ещё больше = even more. Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.en: to finish, to end, to complete
meanings.note: + acc. or infinitive. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'кончить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to finish, to complete', paired with 'заканчивать'.

examples.trans: I want to finish what I started.

examples.text: Был неправ. Простите. Я хочу закончить начатое.
examples.trans: I was wrong. Forgive me. I want to finish what I started.

meanings.note: Opposite of открытый. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крытый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('closed').

examples.trans: I declare the court session closed.

meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: In one direction, now. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.
To run for a second term. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right
А именно = namely. Core Russian part meaning 'exactly, namely, precisely' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: in 'рабочее место' = workplace, job
На его место = in his place. Common neuter noun meaning 'place; seat' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: friendly diminutive of 'минута'; 'я на минуточку' = I'll only be a minute

examples.text: Эдуард Владимирович, я на минуточку. Я спасла монастырь!
examples.trans: Eduard Vladimirovich, I'll only be a minute. I saved the monastery!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'Mikhailovich', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Что за бред? Герман Михайлович просто попросил кофе.
examples.trans: What nonsense is that? German Mikhailovich simply asked for coffee.
German Mikhailovich, Nagiyev has arrived out there.

meanings.note: Short for может быть. Core Russian part meaning 'maybe, perhaps' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I thought maybe you wouldn't see me.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.

examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.en: not for long, for a short time
meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'долго'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I won't be watching TV for much longer.

examples.text: Телевизор мне смотреть недолго. А с Гришкой лежать вечность.
examples.trans: I won't be watching TV for much longer. But I'll be lying next to Grishka for eternity.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job
High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.
What is going on here right now?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to then'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Тогда до одиннадцати, ещё есть вопросы?
examples.trans: Until eleven then, are there any more questions?

examples.text: Герман Михайлович, а нам что сейчас делать?
examples.trans: German Mikhailovich, and what should we do right now?

meanings.note: Остаётся у нас = stays with us. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to stay, to remain', paired with 'остаться'.

examples.trans: And the advance stays with us.

meanings.note: ничего не осталось = there's nothing left

Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remain, to be left', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: From German 'Offiziant' / Late Latin 'officians' (one who performs a duty or service).

examples.trans: The waiter politely greets the new guests.
Please do not block the walkway for the waiters.

meanings.note: Irregular plural повара. Common masculine noun meaning 'cook, chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: On foot. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.en: to be needed, to become necessary
meanings.note: takes dative of person: мне понадобится

examples.text: Этот ключ мне больше не понадобится.
examples.trans: I won't need this key anymore.
If you need help, tell me.

examples.text: Спасибо тебе, Марина. Этот ключ мне больше не понадобится.
examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. I won't need this key anymore.

meanings.note: Asks about the reason. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Рабочее место = job, workplace. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('working; work').
As a noun. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('working; work').

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: свободен! = you're dismissed (a boss to an employee)
свободен! = you're dismissed (a boss to an employee)

examples.trans: That's all, Samson, you can go!

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Смотреть на + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, to watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

TV, a film. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, to watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Его не будет часа два. Вы спокойно всё сделаете.
examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.

meanings.note: the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

meanings.note: In addition. Core Russian adv meaning 'also, as well' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Но людям также нужна высокая культура!
examples.trans: But people also need high culture!

meanings.note: At that time. Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.
Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'бирать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to clean up, to tidy', paired with 'убрать'.
Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'бирать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to clean up, to tidy', paired with 'убрать'.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: How something is done. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
As an answer. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

хотя.gloss: even if, at least (with бы); although

meanings.note: нужно хотя бы поговорить = we need at least to talk
Core Russian part meaning 'even if, at least (with бы); although' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Нужно хотя бы поговорить с ними.
examples.trans: We need at least to talk with them.

examples.text: Вы плохо поступили, но хотя бы совесть есть.
examples.trans: You acted badly, but at least you have a conscience.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
